newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks jumped higher in early Friday trading as the market recovered from the futures-dictated gyrations of Thursday and investors refocused on the positive fundamental outlook, brokers said.
"The correction yesterday was overdone," said Priscilla Ng, executive director of CEF GC Brokerage. "And it was all to do with the futures expiry."
The Hang Seng Index put on 86 points to trade at 13,397.19 after 30 minutes of trade and on healthy turnover of HK$1.13 billion.

The Hang Seng tumbled 220.19 points on Thursday, in active and volatile trade. Both the Hang Seng index and the value of the expiring November Hang Seng Index futures contract underwent a 400-point-plus swings before the close.
Meanwhile, the December contract put on 80 points to trade at 13,480, a slight discount to the cash market.
"Why shouldn't this market go up?" said CEF's Ng. "We should a rerating of the index based on our political stability."
Technical analysts were divided on whether the market had undergone a sufficient correction in intraday trading Thursday.
"The index has already corrected to the 13,300 level," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.

Cheung said the index has established a trading range between 13,300 and 13,800 and if turnover remains at current high levels, he expects to see the index break through the 13,800 level in a week's time.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market followed by utitlies.
Swire Pacific led the blue chips rising HK$1.00 to HK$73.50 buoyed by both the outlook for its property division and a possible fare increase at Cathay Pacific. Cathay was unchanged at HK$12.80.
CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.50 to HK$40.30 and Wharf added HK$0.60 to HK$39.80.

HongKong Telecom gained HK$0.15 to HK$13.40 and China Light advanced HK$0.40 to HK$33.20. Analsyts said both stocks look attractive on a historical valuation basis. Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings gained HK$1.00 to HK$162.00.
Citybus Group Ltd which debuted on Friday, rose to HK$1.60 before easing to HK$1.53. Cheung of J&A Securities said mainland Chinese institutions and individuals were active in new issues.
